700: probably from αἴρω (through the idea of exciting emotion); to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so):--please.
701: from ἀρέσκω; agreeable; by implication, fit:--(things that) please(-ing), reason.
702: of foreign origin; Aretas, an Arabian:--Aretas.
703: from the same as ἄῤῥην; properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence (intrinsic or attributed):--praise, virtue.
704: perhaps the same as ἄῤῥην; a lamb (as a male):--lamb.
705: from ἀριθμός; to enumerate or count:--number.
706: from αἴρω; a number (as reckoned up):--number.
707: of Hebrew origin (רָמָה); Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in Palestine:--Arimathæa.
708: from the same as ἄριστον and ἄρχω; best ruling; Aristarchus, a Macedonian:--Aristarchus.
709: from ἄριστον; to take the principle meal:--dine.
710: apparently a comparative of the same as ἄριστον; the left hand (as second-best):--left (hand).
711: from the same as ἄριστον and βουλή; best counselling; Aristoboulus, a Christian:--Aristobulus.
712: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as ἄῤῥην; the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from ("early")), i.e. luncheon:--dinner.
714: apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to αἴρω through the idea of raising a barrier); properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory):--be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient.
715: probably from ἀρκέω; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity):--bear.
716: probably from αἴρω (perhaps with Α (as a particle of union) prefixed); a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare ἁρμός)):--chariot.
717: of Hebrew origin (הַר and מְגִדּוֹן); Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a symbolic name:--Armageddon.
718: from ἁρμός; to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth):--espouse.
719: from the same as ἅρμα; an articulation (of the body):--joint.
720: perhaps from Α (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of ῥέω; to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate:--deny, refuse.
724: from ἁρπάζω; pillage (properly abstract):--extortion, ravening, spoiling.
726: from a derivative of αἱρέομαι; to seize (in various applications):--catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force).
728: of Hebrew origin (עֲרָבוֹן); a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest:--earnest.
729: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as ῥαφίς; unsewed, i.e. of a single piece:--without seam.
730: probably from αἴρω; male (as stronger for lifting):--male, man.
731: from Α (as a negative particle) and the same as ῥητῶς; unsaid, i.e. (by implication) inexpressible:--unspeakable.
732: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of ῥώννυμι; infirm:--sick (folk, -ly).
733: from ἄῤῥην and κοίτη; a sodomite:--abuser of (that defile) self with mankind.
734: contracted from a compound of Ἄρτεμις and δῶρον; gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian:--Artemas.
735: probably from the same as ἀρτέμων; prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities:--Diana.
736: from a derivative of ἄρτι; properly, something ready (or else more remotely from αἴρω (compare ἄρτος); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel:--mainsail.
737: adverb from a derivative of αἴρω (compare ἄρτος) through the idea of suspension; just now:--this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present.
738: from ἄρτι and γεννητός; just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert:--new born.
739: from ἄρτι; fresh, i.e. (by implication) complete:--perfect.
740: from αἴρω; bread (as raised) or a loaf:--(shew-)bread, loaf.
741: from a presumed derivative of αἴρω; to prepare, i.e. spice (with stimulating condiments):--season.
742: of Hebrew origin (אַרְפַּכְשַׁד); Arphaxad, a post-diluvian patriarch:--Arphaxad.
743: from ἄρχω and ἄγγελος; a chief angel:--archangel.
744: from ἀρχή; original or primeval:--(them of) old (time).
745: from ἄρχω and Λαοδικεύς; people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish king:--Archelaus.
746: from ἄρχομαι; (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank):--beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule.
747: from ἀρχή and ἄγω; a chief leader:--author, captain, prince.
748: from ἀρχή and a derivative of ἱερός; high-priestly:--of the high-priest.
749: from ἀρχή and ἱερεύς; the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest:--chief (high) priest, chief of the priests.
750: from ἀρχή and ποιμήν; a head shepherd:--chief shepherd.
751: from ἀρχή and ἵππος; horse-ruler; Archippus, a Christian:--Archippus.
752: from ἀρχή and συναγωγή; director of the synagogue services:--(chief) ruler of the synagogue.
753: from ἀρχή and τέκτων; a chief constructor, i.e. "architect":--masterbuilder.
754: from ἀρχή and τελώνης; a principle tax-gatherer:--chief among the publicans.
755: from ἀρχή and a compound of τρεῖς and κλίνω (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches); director of the entertainment:--governor (ruler) of the feast.
756: middle voice of ἄρχω (through the implication, of precedence); to commence (in order of time):--(rehearse from the) begin(-ning).
757: a primary verb; to be first (in political rank or power):--reign (rule) over.
758: present participle of ἄρχω; a first (in rank or power):--chief (ruler), magistrate, prince, ruler.
759: from αἴρω (in the sense of sending off scent); an aromatic:--(sweet) spice.
760: of Hebrew origin (אָסָא); Asa, an Israelite:--Asa.
761: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of σαλεύω; unshaken, i.e. (by implication) immovable (figuratively):--which cannot be moved, unmovable.
762: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of σβέννυμι; not extinguished, i.e. (by implication) perpetual:--not to be quenched, unquenchable.
763: from ἀσεβής; impiety, i.e. (by implication) wickedness:--ungodly(-liness).
764: from ἀσεβής; to be (by implied act) impious or wicked:--commit (live, that after should live) ungodly.
765: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of σέβομαι; irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked:-- ungodly (man).
766: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other vices):--filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness.
767: from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of σημαίνω; unmarked, i.e. (figuratively) ignoble:--mean.
768: of Hebrew origin (אָשֵׁר); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe:--Aser.
769: from ἀσθενής; feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty:--disease, infirmity, sickness, weakness.
770: from ἀσθενής; to be feeble (in any sense):--be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.
771: from ἀσθενέω; a scruple of conscience:--infirmity.
772: from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of σθενόω; strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral):--more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing).
773: of uncertain derivation; Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore:--Asia.
774: from Ἀσία; an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia:--of Asia.
775: from Ἀσία and ἀρχή; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor:--chief of Asia.
777: from Α (as a negative particle) and σῖτος; without (taking) food:--fasting.
778: probably from the same as σκεῦος; to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive):--exercise.
779: from the same as ἀσκέω; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle:--bottle.
780: adverb from a derivative of the base of ἡδονή; with pleasure:--gladly.
781: from Α (as a negative particle) and σοφός; unwise:--fool.
782: from Α (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of σπάω; to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome:--embrace, greet, salute, take leave.
783: from ἀσπάζομαι; a greeting (in person or by letter):--greeting, salutation.
784: from Α (as a negative particle) and σπιλόω; unblemished (physically or morally):--without spot, unspotted.
785: of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp":--asp.
786: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of σπένδω; literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless:--implacable, truce-breaker.
787: of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin:--farthing.
788: neuter comparative of the base of ἐγγύς; more nearly, i.e. very near:--close.
789: probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia MInor:--Assos.
790: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of ἵστημι; to be non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless:--have no certain dwelling-place.
791: from (a city); urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome:--fair.
792: probably from the base of στρώννυμι; a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively:--star.
793: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of στηρίζω; unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating:--unstable.
794: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of (to cherish affectionately); hard-hearted towards kindred:--without natural affection.
795: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and (an aim); to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth:--err, swerve.
796: from ἀστράπτω; lightning; by analogy, glare:--lightning, bright shining.
797: probably from ἀστήρ; to flash as lightning:--lighten, shine.
798: neuter from ἀστήρ; properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial):--star.
799: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of συγκρίνω; incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian:--Asyncritos.
